stories.title: Media Outlets Sue Trump Administration Over White House Coverage Ban
stories.summary: CNN, Politico, and MS NOW have announced plans to sue the Trump administration after being banned from White House coverage. The outlets argue that the ban is unconstitutional and a violation of the First Amendment. Following the ban, other major networks have also declined to provide pool coverage of President Trump's activities.

stories.summary: Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and businessman Rande Gerber, has died at the age of 27. His death occurred at a rehabilitation facility in Los Angeles, as confirmed by a family representative. The family has requested privacy during this difficult time.

stories.title: Ukraine Launches Massive Drone Attack on Moscow, Causing Casualties and Damage
stories.summary: Ukraine has launched a significant drone attack involving over 1,000 drones targeting Russia, marking the largest assault on Moscow to date. The attack coincided with the final day of tightly controlled parliamentary elections in Russia. Reports indicate that the assault resulted in damage to an oil refinery and a residential building, with at least two fatalities confirmed in Moscow. The mayor of Moscow described the event as the largest drone attack on the city.

stories.summary: Paramount has reached a settlement with California and 11 other states, resolving a lawsuit that challenged its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. This agreement allows the merger to proceed, removing a significant legal obstacle for Paramount's acquisition plans.

stories.title: Pakistan Claims Airstrikes in Afghanistan Kill 28 Militants; Afghanistan Reports Civilian Casualties
stories.summary: Pakistan reported that airstrikes in Afghanistan resulted in the deaths of 28 militants in the border provinces of Kunar and Paktika. In contrast, Afghan authorities stated that three civilians were killed in the strikes. This incident follows a recent attack on police in Kohat, Pakistan.

stories.title: Putin's United Russia Party Secures Majority in Parliamentary Elections
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin's ruling United Russia party has achieved a record majority in the recent parliamentary elections, winning approximately 58% of the vote. The elections, which have faced criticism for being tightly controlled, resulted in United Russia securing 355 out of 450 seats in the Duma. Additionally, 49 veterans of the Ukraine war were elected to the new parliament, further consolidating the party's influence.

stories.title: UK Charges Man with Genocide-Related Offences from Rwanda
stories.summary: Vincent Brown, also known as Vincent Bajinya, has been charged in the UK with one offence related to genocide and six offences related to murder as a crime against humanity. The 65-year-old is set to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court to face these charges, marking the first prosecution in the UK connected to the 1994 Rwanda genocide.

stories.title: China Expels Two Senior Military Leaders Amid Anti-Corruption Drive
stories.summary: China has expelled two high-ranking generals from the Communist Party due to allegations of corruption and disloyalty. This action is part of an ongoing anti-corruption campaign within the military. One of the expelled leaders, Zhang Youxia, was the highest-ranked general in the country, serving as a vice chairman on the Central Military Commission.

stories.title: Nigeria Forms Panel to Investigate Deaths of 37 Miners in Custody
stories.summary: The Nigerian government has established a 10-member independent panel to investigate the deaths of 37 suspected illegal gold miners in a holding cell operated by a paramilitary civil defense force. Survivors have described their distressing experiences in detention, while protests erupted in Minna, leading to police deploying tear gas and imposing a curfew. Families of the deceased are demanding justice following the incident.

stories.title: Google Fined €403 Million by Irish Data Watchdog for GDPR Violations
stories.summary: Google has been fined €403 million by Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC) for violations related to the processing of users' location data. The fine follows an inquiry initiated six years ago, prompted by complaints from various European consumer rights organizations. The DPC found that users may not have been adequately informed about how their location data was used for targeted advertising.

stories.summary: Charles Spencer, the brother of Princess Diana, has accused King Charles III of 'gaslighting' him regarding his recollections of events surrounding Diana's death. This accusation comes ahead of the release of Spencer's memoir, where he claims the King was 'giddily elated' shortly after Diana's passing. The controversy has sparked significant discussion in the UK as the memoir's publication approaches.

stories.title: Kremlin Party Secures 355 Seats in Russian Parliament Amid Controversial Elections
stories.summary: In recent parliamentary elections, Russia's pro-Putin party achieved a record 355 seats, maintaining its dominance in the State Duma. The elections were characterized by allegations of being tightly controlled, with an anti-war party failing to meet the threshold for representation. Reports indicate that the voting process was heavily monitored, including instances of armed soldiers overseeing ballot submissions.

stories.title: Typhoon Dujuan prompts evacuation orders for millions in Japan
stories.summary: Japan's Meteorological Agency has issued warnings of an 'imminent threat to life' as Typhoon Dujuan approaches. Nearly two million people across six prefectures, including Tokyo, have been urged to evacuate. Although the threat level has been downgraded in most areas, authorities continue to emphasize the need for caution.
